claims.statement: EU food-information law requires listed allergens to be declared and requires upstream businesses supplying non-final food to pass enough information onward for downstream compliance.
EU food businesses must maintain traceability procedures and withdraw unsafe food, creating a durable need for controlled change records.
The Commission's food-safety-management notice treats allergen control as a food-safety-management requirement, but qualified operators remain responsible for HACCP and release decisions.
The reachable sector is large but fragmented: Eurostat reports 4.7 million EU food-and-beverage-processing workers and EUR266 billion of value added in 2022.
Incumbents already advertise supplier portals, version control, BOM linkage, allergen propagation and recipe-to-label impact analysis, so a generic specification repository is not differentiated.

A viable wedge is therefore an integration-first SME exception-clearing service distributed by ingredient distributors or auditors, not a replacement PLM; channel willingness and paid demand remain unverified.

contrary_evidence: TraceGains, Specright, FoodChain ID and Foods Connected publicly offer most core graph, change-control and allergen-impact functions.
The public RASFF interface omits commercial identities, limiting its value for supplier-level incident linkage.
No public evidence establishes distributor feed rights, channel economics or SME willingness to pay per cleared change.

economics.acquisition_route: Test one-to-many resale through a regional ingredient distributor or certification auditor; direct SME sales are a fallback only for the first five paid pilots.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Planning case, not validated: 300 sites at 1800 PLN blended monthly revenue is 6.48 million PLN ARR; at 20% operating margin and retained founder control, several profitable years could support more than 5 million PLN of founder equity and accumulated cash. The site count, price and valuation multiple all require validation.
economics.founder_time: About 3 founder hours daily for parsing, graph logic and partner operations; a contracted food-safety professional must review exceptions and release design.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Planning range of 65-75% after document processing, human exception review, support and channel share; no observed vendor cost or margin evidence supports it yet.
economics.payback: Unknown until a paid pilot measures onboarding effort and partner share; require projected first-year gross profit to exceed acquisition and connector cost before scaling.
economics.pricing: Test 10000 PLN onboarding, 1200 PLN per site-month and 300 PLN per human-cleared specification-change report; these are hypotheses, not observed market prices.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Supplier, formulation, allergen, packaging or label changes recur, but retention depends on becoming the accepted audit trail rather than a duplicate PLM.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Contractually permissioned change decisions, false-positive resolutions and remediation outcomes improve exception prioritisation without repurposing confidential formulas
fingerprint.customer: Small and mid-sized EU food manufacturers lacking an integrated PLM change-control layer
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embedded connector and partner-branded alerting through ingredient distributors and certification auditors
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Ingredient-to-label dependency and exception-clearance layer sold per site, onboarding and cleared change
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The manufacturer pays for an active site and when a specification change receives a documented human-cleared impact report
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An ingredient supplier changes composition, process, allergen declaration, origin or specification version

founder_fit: Document parsing, dependency modelling and exception scoring fit the founder's data-science and AI leverage.
A channel-led product can be operated part-time initially, but food-safety release authority must remain with qualified customer personnel or contracted experts.
Enterprise integration and partner development add sales load but can be bounded to a few repeatable channels.
risks: A missed allergen dependency could harm consumers; the product must never auto-release labels and needs immutable audit trails, access control and professional review.
Incumbent PLM vendors can bundle the functionality or block integrations.
Supplier specifications and formulas are commercially sensitive; contracts must grant narrowly scoped processing and derived-data rights.

structure.control_point: The approved dependency and exception trail from supplier specification through recipe, label and release decision
structure.critical_dependency: Timely structured supplier specifications, integration rights, and qualified human release ownership

thesis: Embed a narrow supplier-specification change and exception-clearance layer with ingredient distributors or food auditors for EU SMEs that lack integrated PLM, charging by site and cleared change while preserving qualified human release approval.
title: AllergenChange Supplier Graph
uncertainties: Whether distributors or auditors will provide timely feeds and resale access under reusable rights.
Whether SMEs will pay separately when incumbent PLM, retailer portals or spreadsheets already cover the workflow.
Document extraction accuracy and the human-review burden across languages and inconsistent supplier formats.
Insurance, security and integration costs at regulated production scale.
